Technical Program Manager

About Us

OpenFX is on a mission to move money as freely as data, unrestricted by time zones, banking hours, or legacy systems. We are building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of cross-border payment systems for institutions. The team's execution has been exceptional, and we're scaling at a remarkable pace. Our stellar early team comes with experience in companies like J. P. Morgan, Goldman Sachs, FalconX, Paypal, Affirm, Polygon, Kraken, Nium & others. We're backed by Accel, Faction, NfX, Accomplice, and other top-tier investors.

Role Overview

You will run the weekly heartbeat of engineering delivery. Sprint planning support across pods, release train readiness checks ahead of every go live, cross pod sync, and the escalation path when something breaks. You will make sure every ceremony answers exactly one question, and you will split the ones that have quietly turned into two.

You will chase the details that others let slide. Stale tickets. Unowned dependencies. Target dates that do not line up with a deployment train. Story points that never rolled up to the epic. Acceptance criteria that were never written. This is unglamorous work and it is the difference between a quarter that lands and one that does not.

You will own the RAID log and act on it. Risks, assumptions, issues, and dependencies get a named owner and a date, and you follow up until they close. When an owner goes quiet, you go find them.

You will produce the reporting the org runs on. The Engineering Daily Brief, the Monthly Business Review, and the Quarterly Business Review. You will pull the data yourself, verify it against the source rather than taking a dashboard at face value, and flag the exceptions before anyone has to ask.

You will keep the delivery system clean. Linear project configuration, workflows, board hygiene, automation rules, capacity plans, deployment calendars, and Notion documentation. If the data going in is sloppy, every report downstream is a guess.

You will coordinate the programmes that cross pod boundaries. Settlement rail expansions, banking partner integrations, platform migrations, and the regulatory workstreamsthat come with operating under GDPR and licensing. You will sequence the work, hold the timeline, and run the standing forum where blockers get resolved.

You will be the single point of truth on delivery status. When something is off track, leadership hears it from you first, with the cause, the options, and a recommendation. Not a colour on a slide.

You will work across the whole org. Engineering Managers, Product, QA, DevOps, InfoSec, and Compliance, plus counterparts in the US and Netherlands. Most of your influence comes without authority, which means it comes from being reliably useful and from following through every single time.

Minimum Qualifications

● 6+ years in technical program management, delivery management, scrum mastery at scale, or a comparable execution focused role in a software organisation.

● Demonstrated ownership of delivery across multiple engineering teams at once, including planning, tracking, and reporting.

● Strong hands on command of Linear or Jira. You can configure projects, build boards and workflows, write automation rules, and construct a JQL query without help.

● Fluency with agile delivery in practice rather than in theory. You know what a sprint commitment is worth and what to do when a team is going to miss it.

● Technical literacy sufficient to follow engineering discussions, ask sharp questions, and summarise the outcome accurately. You do not need to write the code. You do need to understand what is being built and why it is hard.

● Excellent written communication. You can compress a messy 40 minute discussion into a paragraph an executive can act on.

● Comfort with data and spreadsheets. You would rather pull the numbers yourself than wait a week for someone else to.

Preferred Qualifications

● Background in payments, cross border FX, banking, or another regulated financial domain.

● Experience running release trains, deployment calendars, or change management processes in an environment with real production risk.

● Experience coordinating vendor and third party integrations, including onboarding and security review timelines.

● Experience with Notion, Linear, or similar tooling, and with migrations between delivery systems.

● A bias toward the smallest process that works. We measure this role by the risks it retires and the dates it protects, not by the artifacts it produces.

Additional Requirements

● This role is based in Bengaluru and works closely with colleagues in the US and the Netherlands. Expect some overlap with different working hours.

About the Company

Rain is the global stablecoin payments platform for enterprises, neobanks, platforms, developers, and AI agents. Our technology allows partners to move, store, and use stablecoins instantly and compliantly through global payment cards, rewards, on/offramps, wallets, and cross-border rails. As both a Visa and Mastercard Principal Member, Rain issues cards that work at more than 175 million merchant locations in over 220 countries and territories. Built natively for stablecoins and trusted by more than 100 organizations worldwide, Rain delivers secure, scalable infrastructure that makes money move freely and instantly around the world.

You will have the opportunity to deliver massive impact at a hypergrowth company backed by some of the top investors in fintech, crypto, and SaaS. In January 2026, we closed a $250M Series C led by ICONIQ, valuing Rain at $1.95B, with Sapphire Ventures, Norwest, Galaxy Ventures, Dragonfly, Bessemer Venture Partners, FirstMark, Lightspeed, and Endeavor Catalyst also participating. If you're curious, bold, and excited to help shape a borderless financial future, we'd love to talk.

Our Ethos

We believe in an open and flat structure. You will be able to grow into the role that most aligns with your goals. Our team members at all levels have the freedom to explore ideas and impact the roadmap and vision of our company.

About the role

Rain is building payments and stablecoin infrastructure. Every transaction generates data across our system.

We’re looking for an Analytics Engineer, Finance to own the data layer Finance runs on: model it, reconcile it against source systems, test it, automate it, and make it self-serve. You’ll partner with Finance and Accounting and the data team to make sure every number we report ties back to its source.

We’re looking for someone with high agency and urgency who owns problems end to end, digs into discrepancies until the numbers tie out, and communicates clearly when something is uncertain. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built.

At Rain, we’re builders who use AI to automate repetitive work. That changes what data roles look like: where a data scientist used to only analyze and an analyst used to only build dashboards, here everyone models data, writes production-quality code, and automates their own workflows. You own the result, including checking what the AI produces. For this role, that means building trusted models and automating the reconciliations and reporting Finance depends on.

What you’ll do

Operability Design Review
Review controls designs, including BMS/BAS, EPMS, SCADA, PLC-based plant controls, CDU and cooling plant controls, and generator, UPS, and switchgear controller integration, through an operations lens. Provide QA/QC oversight of controls scope for new construction and retrofits: review vendor proposals and programming, directly oversee system configuration and component upgrades, and witness factory tests. Verify controls turnover packages: as-built sequences of operation, point lists, control and network drawings, programming backups and configuration files under version control, licenses and credentials transferred to Hut 8, alarm setpoint and priority matrices, trend baselines, spare controllers and critical modules, and PM program inputs such as backup routines, firmware updates, and panel power health. Provide technical controls training and support to Facility Operations staff, and validate that operator training equips the team to use the systems, not just look at them.
